name: UK Parliament Hackathon with EasyA
theme: Technology, AI, blockchain, and government in a UK Parliament pitch setting.
build_window: Projects may start from 2026-08-24; pitch day is 2026-09-04.
required_tech: AI and/or crypto/blockchain must be material to the core product path.

requirements.description: Projects must be AI and/or crypto/blockchain, and the AI or crypto mechanism must be core rather than incidental.
Teams may have at most 5 people.
Participants present or pitch on 2026-09-04 in Parliament before MPs, civil servants, and invited guests.
Participants may begin building from 2026-08-24; the event day is a pitch format rather than a multi-hour coding session.
The event is open to people regardless of technical experience, including non-coders, university students, and seasoned developers.
A special prize is dedicated for non-coders.
No specific model, blockchain, sponsor SDK, or repository format is stated as mandatory in the supplied evidence.

submission_artifacts: Working live or recorded demo is described as strategically important, but no formal repository, deck, video, model, or written report requirement is published in the supplied evidence.
demo_requirements: On-the-day pitch in front of MPs, civil servants, and invited guests.
A working demo understandable to a non-technical parliamentarian is described as the submission that matters, but no formal demo specification is published.
prizes: Prize money: equity-free funding for the best projects.
Grants: hundreds of thousands in follow-on grant funding for winning projects.
Exact prize amounts are not published in the supplied evidence.

Participants may start building from Monday 24 August 2026; pitch day is 4 September 2026.

sanitized_brief: UK Parliament Hackathon with EasyA is an in-person pitch competition scheduled for 2026-09-04, 12:30-17:30, at the House of Commons in London. Participants may start building from 2026-08-24. Teams are limited to 5 people. Projects must use AI and/or crypto/blockchain as a material core mechanism; no specific model, chain, SDK, repository, dataset, or sponsor technology is stated as mandatory. The event is open to non-coders as well as developers, and a special non-coder prize is stated. No published scoring rubric, track list, exact prize amounts, or formal artifact checklist is available in the supplied evidence. The event format is a pitch before MPs, Lords, civil servants, and invited guests; demo clarity for non-technical parliamentarians, parliamentary relevance, and AI/crypto substance are inferred as important but not published as weighted criteria. Useful capabilities include EasyA's Web3/developer community, workshops, venue access, and exposure to government decision-makers, startups, recruiters, and VCs. Crowding labels: high collision includes generic AI wrappers, PDF summarizers, dashboard-only analytics, and recommendation lists without action; medium collision includes benefits/grant navigators and generic opportunity boards; potentially underexplored areas include appeal-pathway reconstruction, official-rule resource allocation, administrative error prevention, eligibility inconsistency detection, procedural fairness simulation, and demonstration failure-surface minimisation.
